content.comment_body: Hello, I purchased a [product_name] and connected a 24V switch to input I1. My program uses a timer so that when the switch is closed, output Q1 is activated after one second. I've hooked up a 24V solenoid to output Q1, but it doesn't respond at all. Does anyone know what might be causing this?

Have you checked the online test to confirm whether your input and output are actually being activated? You can also verify the I/O status display on the [product_name]. Could you provide more details about your wiring setup?

Yes, I checked the online test. The input was activating but kept turning off and on repeatedly for some unexplained reason. I heard a clicking inside the device previously and thought it might be faulty, but now there's no noise. Regarding wiring: I connected a cable from an external 24V supply to the N/O contact, then from the other N/O contact to input I1 on the [product_name]. For output Q1, I connected my solenoid using the two red wires straight to the two terminals on Q1, regardless of polarity. Is this correct?

Hello, The [product_name] has 4 high-speed counter inputs and 4 analog inputs. Note that: I1 = AI3 (analog input), I2 = AI4 (analog input), I7 = AI1 (analog input), and I8 = AI2 (analog input). This information may help clarify your configuration. Best regards, [user_name]
Would using I3 instead make the output remain activated steadily?

Hi, For wiring the inputs: Use the terminal 'P' on the [product_name] power supply, pass it through your switch, and then connect it to I1. The [product_name] has 8 inputs, 4 of which (I1, I2, I7 & I8) can be set as either digital or analog inputs, but not both simultaneously. The issue may be with the wiring at the output. The 'RC' in the name indicates Relay and Clock. If nothing is connected at the output and you enable the switch, you'll hear the relay close but no voltage is provided—you need to supply power and use the relay contact in the output to complete the circuit for your load. Unlike some versions that have transistor outputs supplying 24V 0.3A directly, relay outputs simply close the circuit. Hope this helps.

When I run the program in the online simulation, the input toggles on and off constantly. Is that normal, or could the online program be lagging behind real time? I have a 24V supply connected to terminal 2 of output Q1; one red wire from my solenoid goes to terminal 1 of Q1, and the other to ground. The solenoid still isn't working. Could the [product_name] be defective?
Try to find a sample program and wiring diagram related to your setup. Make sure your power supply meets the solenoid's power requirements. Best of luck!

Just a note: You need to connect power properly. Run a wire from the power source to Q1-1, connect one wire from the solenoid to Q1-2, and the other wire from the solenoid to the negative power terminal.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges in wiring and setting up the [product_name] for output voltage control, particularly with relay output modes. There is confusion about distinguishing relay vs transistor output terminals, configuring analog and digital inputs, and properly routing power through relay contacts to drive external loads. Since there is no error feedback, troubleshooting centers on the lack of solenoid activation. Users also struggle with recognizing hardware version differences and interpreting I/O status during programming and simulation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the input to reliably activate the output, delivering 24V to operate a solenoid and for the logic and I/O status indications to be consistent and clear. They also expect straightforward configuration of input and output modes with minimal confusion.
